steps.title: “Pay only €30 this month”
steps.body: When you pay less than the full card bill, the rest rolls into the next month: [[revolving-credit]]. In Germany, rolled-over card debt often costs 15–20% a year. The minimum payment keeps you paying for a long time.

stat.label: still owed on a €1,000 bill after a year of minimum payments

steps.prompt: How do you handle a €1,000 card bill? Pick one and see what's left to pay over a year.

choices.label: Pay it all now
choices.ending: Done in one month, nothing extra paid. It may mean a tighter month.

choices.label: Pay the minimum every month
choices.ending: After a year you have paid about €340 and still owe €830. At 18% a year, most of each payment covers interest.

choices.label: Switch to a 12-month instalment plan at 8%
choices.ending: €87 a month. The debt is gone in a year, and you paid about €1,044 for a €1,000 bill.

steps.prompt: You pay only the minimum for a year. Why is most of the bill still there?
options: Interest is added to what's left each month, so much of each payment covers interest
The minimum payment is a fee, not a repayment
The card adds new purchases automatically
steps.explanation: At 1.5% a month, a €1,000 balance costs €15 a month in interest. A €30 payment only cuts half of that off the debt.

steps.prompt: Which works like compound growth on savings, but against you?
steps.explanation: [[compound-interest]] grows savings on top of earlier growth. Rolled-over debt grows on top of earlier interest, the same maths in reverse.
